messages.author: 8ffd6137fd43c6df
messages.subject: works intermittently
parts:
I have a small Shiny app that loads to completion about 5% of the time on a Red Hat server hosted by our Campus IT (http://shiny.ouhsc.edu/SdtThreshold/).  The nonreactive parts of the UI always load, but the parts (eg, graphs & tables) that need calculations rarely complete.  When they do complete, there's typically a 20+ sec delay.  There's no pattern I can determine.  Hitting F5 a few times and waiting is what I'm trying.

The app loads quickly on a 3 development machines (2 Win8 and 1 Ubuntu) and on ShinyApps.io (http://wibeasley.shinyapps.io/SdtThreshold/).  The virtual server has plenty of resources (and I'm also looking at the `top` output).

There's nothing in the Shiny error logs  (http://rstudio.github.io/shiny-server/latest/#application-error-logs) other than the packages loading. 

Other than the OS, the only difference is it's running R 3.1.0 (which is the latest on EPEL), while the others are 3.1.1 or 3.1.1-patched.  The code is on GitHub (https://github.com/OuhscBbmc/SdtThreshold).

Does someone have ideas what could be causing this, or what I can try next?  -Will

messages.author: 8ffd6137fd43c6df
messages.subject: Re: works intermittently
parts:
I think this involves some weird interaction with ggplot2.  Debugging got a little easier when I increased the time out values (eg, https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/shiny-discuss/tUcEMk1Av8Y), and it was clearer that my syntax wasn't incorrect, but instead was how I was using it.  Or how the server is configured.  These plots render within 5 sec on any underpowered laptop, and even on the server when I launch it through RStudio Server's "Run App" button (ie, http://10.27.128.95:8787/p/6488/).  

The response times have a lot of noise; the same code will sometimes take 3 sec, and sometimes take 26.  I have the "Disable cache" box checked in Chrome's dev tools.  IE's no faster.  I can't determine what's code makes it slower, but I'm pretty sure more elements in a ggplot make the Shiny page render slower.  And when I add a second graph, it takes more than 60 sec.

Is this related to some networking issue on our campus?  I don't understand why it seems to be interacting with the complexity of a plot. Any suggestions what network config settings I should ask Campus IT examine first?
